core:28:word:10.reason: Preserve the Mexican pan dulce as the answer; its English support supplies the food gloss separately.

core:28:word:15.priorEnglish: And what did you do for a living?
core:28:word:15.sourceEnglish: And what do you do for a living?
core:28:word:15.targetFrenchDraft: Et vous, que faites-vous dans la vie ?
core:28:word:15.reason: Preserve the present-tense occupation question, even though the later story says he formerly taught.

core:28:line:1.priorEnglish: Every morning, Madame Martin, a retired neighbor, has her coffee at the same table.
core:28:line:1.sourceEnglish: Every morning, Don Ramón, a retiree and neighbor from the neighborhood, has his coffee at the same table.
core:28:line:1.targetFrenchDraft: Tous les matins, don Ramón, un voisin retraité du quartier, prend son petit café à la même table.
core:28:line:1.reason: Restore Don Ramón, a male retiree and neighbor; do not substitute Madame Martin.

core:28:line:2.priorEnglish: Today she asks me where I am from, and I tell her: I am from Canada and I am traveling here for two weeks.
core:28:line:2.sourceEnglish: Today he asks me where I'm from, and I tell him: I'm from Canada and I'm here traveling for two weeks.
core:28:line:2.targetFrenchDraft: Aujourd’hui, il me demande d’où je viens, et je lui dis : « Je viens du Canada et je suis ici en voyage pour deux semaines. »
core:28:line:2.reason: Preserve the source tell-him speech act.

core:28:line:3.priorEnglish: Then I ask her: How long have you lived in this neighborhood?
core:28:line:3.sourceEnglish: Then I ask him: How long have you lived in this neighborhood?
core:28:line:3.targetFrenchDraft: Puis je lui demande : « Depuis combien de temps habitez-vous dans ce quartier ? »
core:28:line:3.reason: Restore the male pronoun while retaining the duration question.

core:28:line:4.priorEnglish: She tells me that she has lived here for forty years and used to teach at the school near the square.
core:28:line:4.sourceEnglish: He tells me that he has lived here for 40 years and that he was a teacher at the school on the plaza.
core:28:line:4.targetFrenchDraft: Il me raconte qu’il habite ici depuis quarante ans et qu’il était enseignant à l’école de la place.
core:28:line:4.reason: Echo the source live-here question with the same habiter verb.

core:28:line:5.priorEnglish: Her former work interests me, so I say: Really? Tell me more.
core:28:line:5.sourceEnglish: Since his work interests me, I say: Really? Tell me more.
core:28:line:5.targetFrenchDraft: Comme son travail m’intéresse, je lui dis : « Vraiment ? Racontez-m’en plus. »
core:28:line:5.reason: Restore the male interlocutor without recasting the source as a woman’s former work.

core:28:line:6.priorEnglish: Then she tells me about the market, because on Saturdays they sell very good brioches there.
core:28:line:6.sourceEnglish: Then he talks to me about the market, because on Saturdays they sell very good pan dulce.
core:28:line:6.targetFrenchDraft: Ensuite, il me parle du marché, car le samedi on y vend du très bon pan dulce.
core:28:line:6.reason: Restore the male speaker and pan dulce rather than brioches.

core:28:line:7.priorEnglish: When I ask her what she recommends, she tells me to visit the downtown museum if I have time.
core:28:line:7.sourceEnglish: When I ask him what he recommends, he says that if I have time, I should visit the downtown museum.
core:28:line:7.targetFrenchDraft: Quand je lui demande ce qu’il me recommande, il dit que, si j’ai le temps, je devrais visiter le musée du centre-ville.
core:28:line:7.reason: Restore the male recommendation and downtown museum.

core:28:line:8.priorEnglish: Before leaving, I pay the bill and tell her: It was a pleasure chatting with you.
core:28:line:8.sourceEnglish: Before I leave, I pay the bill and tell him: It was a pleasure chatting with you.
core:28:line:8.targetFrenchDraft: Avant de partir, je paie l’addition et je lui dis : « C’était un plaisir de discuter avec vous. »
core:28:line:8.reason: Preserve the polite source closing and align it with the card.

core:29:word:7.reason: Preserve pan dulce as the answer; the English support supplies sweet bread separately.

core:29:line:1.priorEnglish: After a breakfast of coffee and brioche in a café in Lyon, the server brings the bill to our table.
core:29:line:1.sourceEnglish: After a breakfast of coffee and sweet bread in Oaxaca, the waiter brings the bill to our table.
core:29:line:1.targetFrenchDraft: Après un petit-déjeuner avec du café et du pan dulce à Oaxaca, le serveur apporte l’addition à notre table.
core:29:line:1.reason: Restore Oaxaca and pan dulce rather than a café in Lyon and brioche.

core:29:line:3.priorEnglish: My new friends, Camille and Théo, insist: No, you are our guest today.
core:29:line:3.sourceEnglish: My new friends, Lucía and Andrés, insist: No, here you are our guest.
core:29:line:3.targetFrenchDraft: Mes nouveaux amis, Lucía et Andrés, insistent : « Non, ici, tu es notre invité. »
core:29:line:3.reason: Restore Lucía and Andrés and their direct guest address.

core:29:line:4.priorEnglish: I tell them: No, really, let me pay, but Théo is already handing his card to the server.
core:29:line:4.sourceEnglish: I tell them: No, really, let me pay, but Andrés is already giving cash to the waiter.
core:29:line:4.targetFrenchDraft: Je leur dis : « Non, vraiment, laissez-moi payer », mais Andrés donne déjà des espèces au serveur.
core:29:line:4.reason: Restore Andrés paying cash rather than a substituted friend handing over a card.

core:29:line:6.priorEnglish: Camille answers: Habits vary; if you like, you can ask the server.
core:29:line:6.sourceEnglish: Lucía says that they usually leave 10 percent if the service is good.
core:29:line:6.targetFrenchDraft: Lucía dit qu’ils laissent d’habitude dix pour cent de pourboire si le service est bon.
core:29:line:6.reason: Present Lucía’s reported habit in this Oaxaca scene, conditional on good service, not a universal rule.

core:29:line:7.priorEnglish: I tell them: If you pay the bill, I can offer to leave a tip, and they agree.
core:29:line:7.sourceEnglish: I tell them: If you pay the bill, then I'll leave the tip, and they agree.
core:29:line:7.targetFrenchDraft: Je leur dis : « Si vous payez l’addition, alors c’est moi qui laisse le pourboire », et ils acceptent.
core:29:line:7.reason: Preserve the firm tip offer and acceptance, not a mere proposal to offer.

core:29:line:2.priorEnglish: I take out my card and say: Breakfast is on me today, since you showed me around the city.
core:29:line:2.sourceEnglish: I take out my card and say: Breakfast is on me today, because you showed me the city.
core:29:line:2.targetFrenchDraft: Je sors ma carte et je dis : « Aujourd’hui, le petit-déjeuner, c’est pour moi, parce que vous m’avez fait visiter la ville. »
core:29:line:2.reason: Use a because-equivalent for porque and preserve the city tour.

core:29:line:8.priorEnglish: At the end I say: OK, thanks, but next time it is on me, and everyone laughs.
core:29:line:8.sourceEnglish: At the end I say: OK, thanks, but next time it's on me, and everyone laughs.
core:29:line:8.targetFrenchDraft: À la fin, je dis : « D’accord, merci, mais la prochaine fois c’est pour moi », et tout le monde rit.
core:29:line:8.reason: Restore the exact English support contraction; French meaning is unchanged.
